clue.text: Swine, one who's uninteresting to listen to

indicators.note: listening means we go by how a word is heard rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person; the word heard sounds like the male pig

explanation.surface: Calling someone a swine because they drone on endlessly at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a male pig, and swine is the general word for pigs.

clue.text: Old picture used in autopsy chosen

indicators.note: something used in a phrase sits inside its letters, so the answer is found within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A vintage photograph selected to illustrate a post-mortem report.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old picture' is a film: Hitchcock's 1960 thriller, aptly macabre beside an autopsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Psycho is Alfred Hitchcock's 1960 horror film, and picture is an old-fashioned word for a movie.

clue.text: Various roads set to be overhauled

indicators.note: an overhaul takes something apart and rebuilds it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A council announcement that several roads are scheduled for resurfacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted and various both mean of several different kinds, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: An advantage, being endlessly luxurious

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: plush means rich and luxurious

explanation.surface: Living in endless luxury is presented as a perk.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is a positive point or benefit, the noun use of the word.

clue.text: Strange youth? Very likely

parts.note: odd means strange
a son is a young male

explanation.surface: Asking whether a peculiar youngster is probably what we're dealing with.
explanation.walkthrough: An odds-on chance in betting is one priced so short that it is expected to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds-on is a betting term for a favourite expected to win, so it means highly probable.

clue.text: Last month, F Prefect's friend becoming corrupt!

parts.note: December, abbreviated, is the last month of the year
Arthur Dent, written A Dent, is the friend of Ford Prefect in The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy

explanation.surface: Last month a character from science fiction turned bad.
explanation.walkthrough: Ford Prefect and Arthur Dent are the travelling pair in Douglas Adams's The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy; 'F Prefect' mirrors the initial-plus-surname form A Dent.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes moral decline and self-indulgence, which is a form of corruption.

clue.text: Sounds and smells overwhelming one

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: noses are what smell, and as a verb nose means to smell
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Odours and noises overpowering a single person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds and smells' reads as a pair of nouns; only 'Sounds' is the definition, and 'smells' is the verb-sense of noses.
explanation.definitionFit: Noises are sounds, especially unwanted or loud ones, a plain plural synonym.

clue.text: Women having ideals shattered

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Disillusioned women whose high principles have been dashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies is the polite term for women, a direct plural synonym.

clue.text: Valuable park in very holy surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings enclose whatever is in them, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: pious means devout, deeply religious
a rec (recreation ground) is a British public park or playing field

explanation.surface: A treasured park set in hallowed grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec, short for recreation ground, is the British word for a public park with playing fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious means of great worth or value, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Head of science to take up chair

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
to eat is to take up food, consume it

explanation.surface: The head of a science faculty being appointed to a professorial chair.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an academic taking up a chair; 'chair' is just furniture here.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat is anything to sit on, and a chair is one such piece of furniture.

clue.text: Skilful band or society regularly appearing

indicators.note: appearing at regular intervals means every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A talented musical band or club that turns up on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means deft and clever with hands or mind, a synonym for skilful.

clue.text: Remove dogsled I damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: all the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A musher confessing to breaking a sled and asking for it to be taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge is to force something out of its position, so it means remove.

clue.text: Information concerning class

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Details about which category something belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is informal British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or kind, especially of art or literature, so a class.

clue.text: Kaput goes vast heater!

indicators.note: kaput means broken down, so the letters fall apart and are rebuilt

parts.note: every letter of both words

explanation.surface: A huge heater breaks down with a cry of dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas stove burns gas for cooking or warmth, so it is a kind of heater.

clue.text: Reading or writing, perhaps, in each period

indicators.note: one item placed in another means it is put inside it

parts.note: ea is the abbreviation for each
reading and writing are two of the three Rs of basic education, so each may be R

explanation.surface: Literacy skills considered stage by stage through history.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic; 'perhaps' warns that reading or writing is just an example of an R.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long distinct stretch of history, a synonym for period.

clue.text: Hence cover for firm

parts.note: so means therefore or hence
a lid is a cover for a container

explanation.surface: A business rationale: therefore, insurance protection for the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company in a talk of cover and insurance, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid and firm both describe something hard and stable, not yielding under pressure.

clue.text: Bemoan unconvincing religious books

parts.note: a lame excuse is a weak, unconvincing one
NT stands for the New Testament, a set of religious books

explanation.surface: Complaining about feeble scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament is to express grief or regret, the same verb sense as bemoan.

clue.text: Hustle harassed detective

indicators.note: something harassed is harried and thrown about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: letter for letter

explanation.surface: Pushing and shoving a stressed private investigator.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleuth is an informal word for a detective, someone who tracks down the truth.

clue.text: Journalist having conflict with duke and king

parts.note: ed is short for editor, a journalist
war is armed conflict; having joins it on
D is the abbreviation for duke; with adds it on

explanation.surface: A reporter quarrelling with both a duke and a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: There have been eight English kings named Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward is the name of several English kings, so the answer is a king by example.

clue.text: Wretched person without room

parts.note: w/o is the written shorthand for without
rm is the abbreviation for room

explanation.surface: Pity the poor soul who has nowhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without room' reads like homelessness; it is two abbreviations, w/o and rm, set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Worm is a contemptuous term for a pitiable or despicable person, a figurative sense.

clue.text: Land found by swan swimming with boat

indicators.note: things swimming move about freely, so these letters drift into a new order

parts.note: as written
as written; with adds it to the mix

explanation.surface: An explorer spots a country after a swan paddles alongside the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a landlocked country in southern Africa, and land here means a nation.

clue.text: Accepts Yankee on board public transport

indicators.note: a passenger on board is inside the vehicle, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a bus is public transport
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A transit company lets an American passenger get on.
explanation.walkthrough: To buy an argument or story is informal for believing or accepting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Buys in the informal sense means believes or accepts, as in buying an excuse.

clue.text: Do, re, me, fa, so or la?

definitions.text: Do, re, me, fa, so or la?

parts.words: Do, re, me, fa, so or la?
parts.note: surface reading: a list of short everyday words, a verb, a preposition, a pronoun and so on

parts.words: Do, re, me, fa, so or la?
parts.note: setter's reading: each is a syllable of the tonic sol-fa scale, asking what any one of them is

explanation.walkthrough: Several of these syllables are ordinary words (do, me, so), which disguises the musical scale from The Sound of Music song.
explanation.definitionFit: In sol-fa singing each syllable names one degree of the scale, so each is a single musical tone.

clue.text: After long time, clubs in New York providing service

indicators.note: coming after means the first piece is written at the front, the rest following it

parts.note: an age is a long time

indicators.note: something placed in another thing ends up enclosed by it

parts.note: standard abbreviation for New York
C is clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: Nightclubs in New York finally opening after a long wait to provide a service.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is a business that supplies a particular service, such as a travel or employment agency.

clue.text: Extremely grasping relations in truth

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold within, so the first word clasps the second

parts.note: very means extremely
it is a coy word for sex, sexual relations

explanation.surface: Family members who are very greedy, revealed honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' suggests relatives; here it is sexual relations, which crosswords call IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Verity is a formal word for a true statement or truthfulness, a synonym of truth.
